speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis. To help me understand your condition better, have you noticed any changes in your urination, such as pain, frequency, or the color of your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fever and flank pain persisting after your sinusitis treatment are concerning for a new infection. Given your history, have you noticed any urgency, frequency, or burning when you urinate?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is interesting; the rash could indicate an allergy to penicillin-class antibiotics or a specific bacterial infection like *E. coli* O157:H7. Did the flank pain move to your groin or genitals, and have you noticed any unusual discharge from those areas? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture & Sensitivity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS) Syndrome.

The presence of binucleated eosinophilic cells on the cytospin, combined with your history of a rash and systemic symptoms after antibiotics, points to a severe drug reaction rather than a simple urinary tract infection. Please stop all non-essential medications immediately and return to the emergency department for monitoring of organ function.
